Wonty Privacy Policy

Effective date: November 18, 2026

Wonty is an app for keeping your wishes in one place, grouping them into catalogs, sharing them with friends, reserving gifts for each other and organizing events such as birthdays and Secret Santa.

This policy explains what personal data Wonty handles, how and why, who else receives it, how long it is kept, and how you can see, change or delete it. We have tried to write it in plain language. If anything is unclear, write to us at krasovskyi.yevhenii@gmail.com.

The short version

  • You can use Wonty without an account. Everything then stays on your phone, and we don't receive it. Only the websites whose links you add are contacted, directly by your phone (section 4).
  • With an account, your account details, wishes, catalogs and pictures are stored with our hosting provider, Supabase, in a data center in Ireland (EU), so they are backed up, synced across your devices and can be shared with the people you choose.
  • No ads, no analytics, no tracking. Wonty contains no advertising, analytics or crash-reporting tools, doesn't track you across other apps or websites, and we don't sell your data.
  • Other people see only what you share with them. By default, the owner of a wish can't see who reserved it, or whether anyone did. In a Secret Santa draw, each person sees only the one person they give a gift to.
  • You can delete your account and its data in the app, at any time: Settings > Account > Delete Account. A few technical records stay for a limited time (section 11).

2. Using Wonty without an account

You can keep your wishes and catalogs in Wonty without an account ("guest mode"). In guest mode, everything you create is stored only on your phone, inside the app's private storage:

  • your wishes: title, note, link, price and currency, category, status (for example "fulfilled"), favorite mark and picture;
  • your catalogs: name, description, icon, cover picture, which wishes they contain, and your reservation setting;
  • pictures you add: Wonty saves a resized copy (JPEG, at most 1280 pixels on the longer side);
  • app settings, such as appearance and default currency;
  • an invitation link you opened, until you finish setting up the app or signing in.

We don't receive any of this. Like other app data, it is included in your iCloud or computer backups if you have turned those on; those backups are managed by you and Apple.

Deleted items. When you delete a wish or a catalog, it disappears from the app, but Wonty keeps a hidden record of it, including its text, link and price, in the app's storage on your phone. Its picture is removed from your phone soon after, usually the next time you open Wonty. If you later create an account, these records are uploaded together with your other data (see section 10).

Deleting the app removes all of this data from your phone.

Even in guest mode, your phone contacts websites directly when you add or open a link. See section 4.

3. Using Wonty with an account

An account lets you back up your data, sync it across your devices, share catalogs, take part in events and reserve gifts. Sharing, events and reservations always need an account.

3.1 Signing in

You can sign in with an email code, with Apple or with Google (the choice offered depends on your device).

  • Email code. You give us your email address, and we email you a 6-digit code that works for 10 minutes. There is no password. When you create an account this way, the app also sends the language it is using (for example "de"), which is stored with your account.
  • Sign in with Apple. Apple confirms who you are and gives us a stable Apple user ID, your email address, and, the first time only, your name. If you choose "Hide My Email", we receive an Apple relay address instead of your real one. If you don't have a name in Wonty yet, the name Apple gives us becomes your name in Wonty. We also keep a token that Apple issues for Wonty. We use it only to tell Apple to disconnect Wonty from your Apple Account when you delete your account.
  • Google. Google confirms who you are and gives us your name, email address, a link to your Google profile picture and a Google user ID. If you don't have a name in Wonty yet, your Google name becomes your name in Wonty. Wonty doesn't use or show your Google picture, but our sign-in service stores the link with your account.

If you sign in with Apple or Google using the same verified email address as an existing Wonty account, both ways of signing in lead to the same account.

When you create an account, the wishes and catalogs already on your phone are added to it, together with the records of items you deleted earlier (see section 2).

3.2 What we store for your account

WhatDetails
AccountEmail address, user ID, how you sign in, the details Apple or Google shared (see 3.1), the language sent at sign-up, and when you signed up and last signed in
SessionsOne per device you are signed in on, with the IP address and the app and device information your phone sends (the "user agent"). This keeps you signed in and protects your account
Your nameThe name other people see (see section 6). It doesn't have to be your real name. You can change it in Settings > Account
Your contentYour wishes, catalogs, catalog contents and categories, as listed in section 2, and their pictures, plus the records of items you deleted (see section 10). If a picture came from a link preview, we also store the web address it came from; only you can see that address
Sharing and events, when you use themShare links and invitations you create, catalogs you joined, events you organize or join, the people you exclude from drawing each other, the wishlists you attach to events, the result of a Secret Santa draw, and your gift reservations. A reservation also includes a short copy of the wish (title, price and the owner's name), which our servers keep as a history of your reservations after the reservation ends (see section 10)

Pictures are stored in private storage. They are shown only to you and to people allowed to see the wish or catalog, through links that expire after one hour.

Wonty doesn't send push notifications at the moment. If we add them, we will update this policy and ask for your permission on your phone first.

3.3 Technical logs

Like any online service, our hosting provider records requests to our servers in technical logs: the IP address (and the country its network provider derives from it), the app and device information your phone sends, the time, and the address of the request, which can include your user ID or the ID of an item. The sign-in service also keeps a security log of sign-ins, sign-outs and account deletions, with the IP address, device information, user ID and email address.

We use these logs only to run Wonty, keep it secure and fix problems. We don't use them for analytics, advertising or profiling. Section 10 explains how long they are kept.

3.4 Do you have to give us this data?

No. You don't need an account to use Wonty. If you want one, we need an email address, or your sign-in with Apple or Google, to create it; without that we can't create the account. To share catalogs, join events or reserve gifts you also need a name in Wonty, so that other people know who you are. Everything else you add, such as notes, prices or pictures, is up to you.

3.5 Data we get from others

Some data about you doesn't come from you directly:

  • Apple or Google, if you sign in with them (see 3.1);
  • other Wonty users: for example, a catalog owner who removes you from their catalog, an event organizer who adds you to a pair of people who can't draw each other (see section 6), or someone who reports your catalog, wish or event, or you, to us (see 3.6).

3.6 Reports

If something you see in Wonty is abusive or wrong, you can tap Report: on a friend's wish, in the menu of a catalog shared with you or of an event you joined, or next to a person in an event. Wonty then opens your email app with a message to us. Below the space for your own words, the message already contains a few reference lines, so that we know where to look: the IDs of what you report and of the person it belongs to (its owner or organizer, or the person you report), and your own user ID. Nothing is sent until you send the email yourself, and you can read and change everything in it first.

If someone reports something of yours, or reports you, we receive from them your user ID and the IDs of the catalog, wish or event concerned, together with what they write. We use reports only to look into misuse (see sections 7 and 14), and we keep them like other messages sent to us (see section 10).

4. Links, previews and other websites

Link previews. When you type or paste a link into a wish, Wonty fetches that page directly from your phone, about half a second after you stop typing, to fill in the title, price and picture for you. This happens on your phone, not on our servers. The website sees your IP address, a generic browser identification and your phone's first language. Wonty sends no cookies with this request and keeps none.

Preview pictures. While you edit a wish, the preview picture is loaded from the website that hosts it. When you save, Wonty downloads a copy and keeps it with your wish. If that download fails, your phone loads the picture from that website each time you look at the wish, until a copy can be saved.

Opening links. When you tap a link in a wish, it opens in a browser like any other visit to that website.

Other people's wishes. Your phone never fetches or previews the links in other people's wishes in the background. It opens them only when you tap them, and it never contacts the address a friend's preview picture originally came from.

These websites are not our service providers. What they do with your visit is governed by their own privacy policies.

5. Your phone: permissions, clipboard and storage

  • Photos. To add a picture, Wonty opens the iOS photo picker. Only the photo you choose is handed to Wonty; the app doesn't browse your photo library.
  • Clipboard. Wonty reads your clipboard only when you tap a Paste button, and uses what you paste only for what you tapped it for, such as the link of a wish. For two days after you first open Wonty, until you open an invitation or close the offer, the app may check whether your clipboard holds a link, without seeing what it is (iOS allows apps to check this). If it does, Wonty offers you, at most twice, a Paste button to open an invitation you may have copied on an invitation page (see section 6.7). It reads the clipboard only if you tap that button. When you tap Copy link, Wonty puts that link on your clipboard.
  • Not used. Wonty doesn't ask for access to your camera, microphone, location, contacts or calendar, doesn't send notifications, and doesn't ask to track you.
  • Your sign-in. Your sign-in session is kept in the app's private storage on your phone. Signing out removes it.

6. What other people can see

Sharing in Wonty works through links. Nothing you create is public: other people see your data only if you share it with them or take part in the same catalog or event, and only after they sign in.

6.1 Your name

Your name in Wonty is visible to:

  • people you share a catalog with;
  • the owner and other members of a catalog you joined;
  • the organizer and other participants of events you join;
  • anyone who opens an invitation link you created, after they sign in (see 6.5).

Other users never see your email address.

6.2 Catalogs you share

When you share a catalog, you get a link. Anyone who has the link and signs in can join, so send it only to people you want to see the catalog. You can see who joined, remove people, and reset the link so the old one stops working. If you share the link through Wonty's share button, the message Wonty prepares includes the catalog's name; it is sent by the app you choose.

People who joined see the catalog's name, description, icon and cover picture, and all its wishes, including fulfilled and archived ones: title, note, link, price, category, status, favorite mark, the date a wish was fulfilled, when it was added or last changed, and the picture. They don't see your other wishes, and they never see the web address a preview picture came from.

6.3 Catalogs you join

The owner can see that you joined. Your name is visible to the owner and the other members, for example next to a gift you reserved (see 6.4). You can leave the catalog at any time.

6.4 Gift reservations

When you reserve a wish, the wish's owner sees only what they chose in the catalog's settings:

Owner's settingWhat the owner sees
Keep it a surprise (default)Nothing. A reserved wish looks exactly like one nobody has reserved
Show what is reservedThat the wish is reserved, but not by whom
Show who reservedWho reserved it, whether it was bought, and when

Wonty always applies the stricter of the setting at the time you reserved and the current one, and tells you before you reserve what the owner will see.

Other people who see the same wish:

  • members of the catalog you reserved through see your name next to the reservation, and whether you marked the gift as bought;
  • in an event without a draw, the other participants see the same;
  • people who see the same wish through a different catalog see only "reserved by someone";
  • in an event with a Secret Santa draw, your name is never shown to anyone: people who can see the same wish elsewhere see only "reserved by someone", and the person receiving the gift never sees the reservation, whatever the setting.

6.5 Invitation previews

Before joining, a signed-in person who has a link sees a preview: for a catalog, its name, icon and the owner's name; for an event, its title, icon, date, type, budget, whether it has a draw and uses wishlists, its status, the organizer's name and the number of participants.

6.6 Events and Secret Santa

The organizer and all participants of an event see:

  • the event details: title, description, icon, cover picture, type, budget, date and status;
  • the list of participants with their names;
  • the pairs of people the organizer excluded from drawing each other (for example couples), if the organizer set any;
  • who attached a wishlist to the event, and which catalog.

Who can see a participant's wishlist:

  • in an event without a draw, all the other participants;
  • in an event with a draw, only the person who drew that participant, and only after the draw.

The Secret Santa draw. The server makes the draw. Each person learns only who they give a gift to. The app never shows the pairs to anyone else, not even the organizer: our database gives each person only their own pair. Some pairs can still be worked out:

  • with only three participants, everyone can work out all the pairs, and Wonty warns about this before the draw;
  • if someone leaves after the draw, the person who was giving to them usually gets their recipient instead, and so learns who the leaver had drawn. If that isn't possible, the organizer is asked to redo the draw.

If the organizer redoes the draw, the old pairs are deleted and all reservations made in the event are cancelled. Names are then drawn again, unless they can't be drawn yet (for example, because fewer than three people are left): then the draw is only reset, and the organizer can draw names later.

If the organizer deletes their account while other people are still in the event, the event passes to the participant who joined first and keeps its title, description and icon. Its cover picture is removed.

6.7 Our website and invitation pages

Invitation links are addresses on our website, which is hosted on GitHub Pages (currently https://wonty-app.github.io). If Wonty is installed on your phone, tapping an invitation link usually opens it straight in the app, without loading our website. Otherwise, a page on our website opens. It shows a general invitation without any details of the catalog or event, and buttons to open or download Wonty. If you tap "Get Wonty", the page copies the invitation link to your clipboard so the app can offer to open it after you install it (see section 5), and then takes you to Apple's App Store.

Like any web host, GitHub receives your IP address and the full address of each page of our website you open, which for an invitation page includes the invitation code. GitHub keeps visitors' IP addresses for security purposes. Our pages set no cookies and use no analytics or advertising.

7. Why we use your data, and our legal bases

If you are in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom or Switzerland, data protection law requires us to name a legal basis for each use of your data.

WhyLegal basis
Creating your account, signing you in (including sending sign-in codes), adding the data already on your phone to your new account, backing up and syncing your dataPerformance of our contract with you (Article 6(1)(b) GDPR)
Sharing catalogs, events, the Secret Santa draw and gift reservationsPerformance of our contract with you (Article 6(1)(b) GDPR)
Keeping sessions, technical logs and security logs; preventing abuse; investigating reports of misuseOur legitimate interest in keeping Wonty secure and working (Article 6(1)(f) GDPR)
Keeping the Apple token so that Wonty can be disconnected from your Apple Account when you delete your accountOur legitimate interest in fully closing your account, as Apple requires (Article 6(1)(f) GDPR)
Running our website and invitation pages (including the visit logs our web host keeps)Our legitimate interest in letting people learn about Wonty and open invitations (Article 6(1)(f) GDPR)
Answering your messages and support requestsOur contract with you, or our legitimate interest in helping you (Article 6(1)(b) or (f) GDPR)
Handling requests about your rights, and meeting other legal dutiesLegal obligation (Article 6(1)(c) GDPR)

We don't use your data for advertising or marketing, and we don't build profiles about you. We don't make decisions about you based solely on automated processing that have legal or similarly significant effects. The Secret Santa draw is a random assignment.

8. Who receives your data

We share data only as described here.

  • Supabase, Inc. hosts Wonty's database, sign-in service, picture storage, server functions, live updates and logs. Your data is stored on Amazon Web Services (AWS) in Ireland. Requests pass through Cloudflare's network, which may also cache pictures for a short time. Our two server functions (the ones that delete accounts and handle Sign in with Apple tokens) may run in the data center closest to you, which can be outside the EU. Supabase is our processor.
  • The email delivery service that sends sign-in codes. It receives your email address and the code. It is our processor, directly or through Supabase.
  • Apple provides Sign in with Apple, the App Store, and the iOS features Wonty uses. When you delete your account, we ask Apple to disconnect Wonty from your Apple Account. If you have allowed your iPhone to share analytics with app developers (iOS Settings > Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements), Apple may give us crash reports and statistics about the app that don't identify you. We use them only to fix problems. Apple handles your data under its own privacy policy: https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/
  • Google, if you sign in with Google, and because our contact address is a Gmail mailbox: every email you send us, such as a support question, a request about your rights or a report (section 3.6), is stored by Google, with your email address and everything the email contains. Google handles your data under its own privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
  • GitHub, Inc. hosts our website and invitation pages (section 6.7), under GitHub's privacy statement: https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/privacy-policies/github-general-privacy-statement
  • Websites you link to, as described in section 4.
  • Other Wonty users, as described in section 6.
  • Authorities, if we are legally required to share data, and only as much as required.

Our processors may use their own sub-processors; Supabase lists its sub-processors at https://supabase.com/legal/subprocessors. Processors may handle your data only on our instructions and are bound by contract to protect it with the same or an equal level of protection as described in this policy. Apple, Google and GitHub act independently under their own policies linked above.

We don't sell your personal data, share it for advertising, or give it to data brokers.

9. International transfers

Your account data is stored in the EU (Ireland). Some recipients are based in, or can access data from, countries outside the European Economic Area, mainly the United States: Supabase, Cloudflare, Apple, Google and GitHub. As described in section 8, our server functions and Supabase's network may also process requests outside the EU.

When data leaves the European Economic Area, we rely on safeguards recognized by EU law: an adequacy decision of the European Commission where one applies (for example the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework for certified companies), or the European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses, such as those in our data processing agreement with Supabase. You can ask us for more information or a copy of these safeguards at krasovskyi.yevhenii@gmail.com.

10. How long we keep your data

  • Your account and content: for as long as you have an account. We don't delete inactive accounts automatically.
  • Things you delete one by one: when you delete a wish, catalog or category, it disappears from all your devices and from everyone you shared it with. To pass the deletion on to your other devices, our servers keep a record of the deleted item, which still includes its content. Nobody else can see it. These records are removed when you delete your account. This also applies to items you deleted on your phone before you created your account: their records are uploaded with your other data when you sign in for the first time. On your phone, the records are removed when you sign out or delete your account (in guest mode, when you delete the app). Pictures of deleted wishes are removed from our storage the next time Wonty syncs, and from your phone soon after, usually the next time you open Wonty.
  • Ended reservations: a reservation ends when you cancel it; when you leave or are removed from the catalog or event; when the wish is deleted or taken out of the catalog; when the catalog or event is deleted; when the wishlist is taken out of the event; when the organizer changes whether the event has a draw or uses wishlists; or when the draw is redone. Our servers then keep its record, with the short copy of the wish (title, price and owner's name), as a history of your reservations, for as long as both accounts exist. Wonty doesn't show this history at the moment; nobody else can see it, and you can ask us to delete it.
  • Catalogs you joined and events you take part in: your membership or participation stays until you leave, the owner or organizer removes you, the catalog or event is deleted, or you delete your account.
  • Old share links and invitations stop working as soon as you reset them. Their records are removed with the event, or when you delete your account.
  • Technical logs: Supabase deletes them automatically after a period set by our hosting plan, at most 90 days.
  • Security log of sign-ins: kept in the logs for at most 90 days, as above. Supabase can also keep a copy of these entries in our database, where deleting your account does not remove them. You can ask us to delete them.
  • Backups: Supabase keeps backups of our database for up to 30 days, depending on our plan. Data you delete disappears from the backups when they expire. Pictures are not part of these backups.
  • Cached pictures: copies held by Supabase's network are cleared within about a minute after a picture is deleted.
  • Messages you send us, including reports: for as long as we need them to help you or to look into a report, and to keep a record of requests about your rights.
  • On your phone: guest data stays until you delete the app (items you delete leave a record, see section 2). Signed-in data stays until you sign out or delete your account.

11. Deleting your data

  • Single items: delete any wish, catalog or category in the app (see section 10 for what remains).
  • Leaving: you can leave a catalog or an event at any time. Leaving ends your access and releases the reservations you made there. Leaving an event also removes your wishlist from it.
  • Signing out (Settings > Account > Sign Out) removes your account's wishes, catalogs and pictures from that phone. They stay in your account and come back when you sign in again. If some changes haven't been uploaded yet, Wonty warns you first.

  • Deleting your account (Settings > Account > Delete Account) is permanent and can't be undone. If you use Sign in with Apple, Apple asks you to confirm. Wonty then:

    1. deletes all your pictures from our storage;
    2. asks Apple to disconnect Wonty from your Apple Account, if you use Sign in with Apple;
    3. deletes your account and everything linked to it: your name, wishes, catalogs, categories (including the records of deleted items), share links, memberships, reservations you made and reservations made on your wishes, event participations, wishlists and your sessions;
    4. removes everything from your phone and signs you out.

    Events you organized that other people are still part of are handed over to another participant (see section 6.6). Events without other participants are deleted.

What can remain after account deletion: technical and security logs, database backups and cached pictures, for the periods in section 10; records held by the email delivery service, Apple and Google about your sign-ins, under their own policies; and short-lived copies on other people's phones, for example a picture in the app's image cache, until their app refreshes. If Wonty could not disconnect your Apple Account, you can do it yourself in your Apple Account settings, under "Sign in with Apple".

In guest mode, deleting a wish or catalog in the app hides it but keeps a record of it on your phone (see section 2). To remove everything, delete the app.

You can also ask us by email at krasovskyi.yevhenii@gmail.com to delete your account or any of your data.

12. Your rights

You have the right to:

  • access your data and get a copy of it;
  • correct it if it's wrong. You can change your name and your content in the app; write to us for anything you can't change yourself, such as your email address;
  • delete it ("right to be forgotten"), in the app or by asking us;
  • restrict how we use it, for example while we check a complaint;
  • data portability: receive the data you gave us in a common, machine-readable format (such as JSON), or have it sent to another service. Wonty has no export button yet, so write to us;
  • object to processing based on our legitimate interests (section 7);
  • withdraw consent at any time where we rely on it (see section 13);
  • complain to a data protection supervisory authority, in particular the authority in Poland, or the one in the country where you live or work, or where you think a violation happened.

To use these rights, write to krasovskyi.yevhenii@gmail.com. We answer within one month. If a request is complex, we may need up to two more months, as the law allows; we will tell you within the first month. To protect your account, we may ask you to write from the email address of your account, or to confirm your request in another way. Using your rights is free.

13. Consent and your choices

Wonty doesn't rely on your consent for the uses described in this policy. If we ever ask for your consent, you can withdraw it at any time; this doesn't affect what we did before.

Your choices:

  • use Wonty without an account, so nothing leaves your phone except the link requests in section 4;
  • sign out on any device, or delete your account in the app;
  • leave catalogs and events, reset share links, and remove people from your catalogs;
  • choose what wish owners see about reservations in each catalog's settings;
  • stop using Sign in with Apple for Wonty in your Apple Account settings, or remove Wonty's access in your Google account. This doesn't delete your Wonty account; use Delete Account for that.

14. Security

  • Connections between the app and our servers are encrypted (HTTPS).
  • Access rules in our database make sure each person can read only what they are allowed to: their own data, and what others shared with them.
  • Pictures are kept in private storage and shown through links that expire after one hour.
  • Share and invitation links contain long random codes that are practically impossible to guess.
  • On your phone, Wonty's data is kept in the app's private storage, protected by iOS.
  • As the operator of Wonty, we can technically access the data stored on our servers, including the results of Secret Santa draws. We access it only when we need to: to keep Wonty running, fix a problem, look into a report of misuse, or answer your request.

No system is perfectly secure. If we learn of a breach that affects your data, we will act and inform you and the authorities as the law requires.

15. Children

Wonty is not directed to children under 13, or under the higher minimum age that applies in their country for using online services without a parent's consent. If you are younger, please don't create an account. If you believe that a child has given us personal data, write to krasovskyi.yevhenii@gmail.com and we will delete it.

16. Changes to this policy

We may update this policy when Wonty changes or the law requires it. We will publish the new version on this page and update the effective date at the top. If a change significantly affects how we use your data, we will let you know clearly, for example in the app or on our website, before it takes effect.
